Charities Aid Foundation appoints James Clarry as new Chief Executive
The Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) has announced the appointment of James Clarry as its Chief Executive.

James Clarry has been Chief Executive of Justice & Care since 2023, a global charity which campaigns to end modern slavery and provides frontline support to exploited people. Before Justice & Care, James was Chief Operating Officer for six years at Coutts, a private bank and wealth manager, following several senior roles across the NatWest Group. James has a background in law and is also Chair of the Board of Fireflai.
James will take on the role from January 2027 at the latest, with Caroline Siarkiewicz continuing as Interim Chief Executive until then.
Sir Edward Braham, Chair of Trustees for the Charities Aid Foundation, said:

"This is a key moment for CAF and its future. James' experience truly reflects the breadth of our organisation, combining a strong background in social purpose, banking and wealth management. He will bring strategic leadership for our teams across the UK and North America, ensuring CAF continues to evolve how we deliver for our clients and support charities and communities in the years ahead.
"I would also like to thank Caroline Siarkiewicz for her diligence and expertise guiding the organisation through this transition."
James Clarry, incoming Chief Executive of the Charities Aid Foundation, comments:

"I am passionate about driving long-term systemic change and believe philanthropy has the power to do so across many areas. CAF is a unique organisation, and I look forward to working with its brilliant teams in the UK and North America to continue delivering for clients, strengthening support for the charity sector, and to help generosity become impact for communities around the world."

For over 100 years, the Charities Aid Foundation has worked at the centre of the giving world, collaborating with corporate and individual donors to enable them to give more effectively, strategically and impactfully. Operating from the UK, US and Canada, CAF distributes over £1 billion annually to social purpose organisations around the world.
